citations.quote: grey-green mould all over the bathroom ceiling and the hallway smells musty
the boiler cuts out at night, bedrooms are cold every morning, heating basically doesn't work at night
the plumber literally said "you need someone who can measure the walls and the ventilation, that's not my job"
I'm going to pay my rent into the official deposit account from November. I've had enough. how do I do that correctly?

plan.because: Required to establish the tenancy and agreed terms.
Required to establish what was reported to the landlord and when.
Required to establish landlord receipt of the defect report.
Required objective evidence of the defect, location and date.
The reported visits need supporting records of responses, proposed work and access.
The mould branch is active; request dated observations at the affected locations.
The heating branch is active; request the inspection and service findings.
Health effects are unmentioned and presumed absent for planning under the silence policy.
A specialist measurement was reported as needed; request any existing technical findings without assuming the cause.
The customer is considering an official rent deposit; the communicated deadline and notice contents are needed to assess safeguards.

questions: When did the mould and heating problems begin, and is there any immediate health or safety risk?
When and how were the defects reported to the landlord, and what repair deadline, if any, was communicated?
Have wall and ventilation measurements or another technical inspection already been carried out?
Has any rent already been deposited, or is this only planned? Which November is intended?
